papers.text: A shed for the prize pumpkin, right where the spotters stand.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Given record (style G11).

papers.text: A lost property box for the bus stop. First item: the bus stop.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Owned gag: lost property. Other: the box goes on the pavement against the draper's window, where the spotters already lean (noses on the glass).

papers.text: Mervyn's bus so far: a bench, a roof, a timetable. Fund the wheels?
papers.subject: inventions
papers.note: Other: Mervyn's bus-so-far stands on the pavement outside the shops.

papers.text: A timetable facing the shop windows. Shoppers miss 60 % of buses.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the board stands in front of the windows.

papers.text: A form for window-shoppers. Tick one: LOOKED, LINGERED, LEANT.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.note: Other: LEANT is the spotters' box (noses on the glass); they mind being counted.

papers.text: A suggestion box for the shops. First suggestion: a nicer box.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.note: Other: the box is fixed to the bus stop post the spotters lean on.

papers.text: Fund Bertram's new watering can. So far: 40 plants, two spotters.
papers.subject: inventions
papers.note: Other: it waters spotters.

papers.text: Turn the hats in the draper's window round. They watch our buses.
papers.subject: hats
papers.note: Sign: the display faces the wall (Shops lose it); refuse: the hats keep watching.

papers.text: Shop doorways for us in drizzle. Our shelter is only roof-shaped.
papers.subject: picnic-weather
papers.note: Other: the Guild loses its doorways to spotters.

papers.text: Lend us the shelter for summer hats. Sign: BUSES ROUND THE BACK.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: A potting shed shelf for a hat. Then a hat stand. Then the shed.
papers.subject: hats
papers.note: The potting shed is the Society's.

papers.text: A duck has filed to nest in our seed trays. Refer it to a shop window box.
papers.subject: ducks
papers.note: Other: the window boxes are the shops'; the duck moves in.

papers.text: The flower bed by the shops, for leeks. Its sign: FLOWERS, EVENTUALLY.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Leeks do flower, in their second year.

papers.text: We will pay for the allotments' ribbon if you cut it in our window.
papers.subject: ribbons
papers.note: Other: the Society's opening moves into a shop window.

papers.text: We would hire the bus shelter for lost umbrellas: FORGOTTEN, BUT OPEN.
papers.subject: picnic-weather
papers.note: A display of lost umbrellas (owned gag) in the shelter; the spotters lose the shelter.

papers.text: We will pay to grow the timetable in cress. Accurate until lunch.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Other: the cress replaces the spotters' printed timetable at the stop.

papers.text: We will pay to put the 9:40 on the map. The map is in the draper's window.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the Guild's window gets a bus route painted on it.

papers.text: Pose by Delphine's self-cleaning window as it works. Allow all day.
papers.subject: inventions
papers.note: Other: a little put out at the favour (gossip).

papers.text: Wear our carrot hat. Rodney says it suits you. He says that of all hats.
papers.subject: hats
papers.note: Callback: Rodney. Other: the Guild, whose hats you did not wear.

papers.text: Our calendar: you at the stop, checking a watch. We can lend one.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the photograph is taken outside the shops, blocking a window (gossip).

papers.text: Lost property is up 40 %: one glove, handed in five times.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The study found the other glove. It asks to study the pair.
papers.note: Owned gag: lost property. Other: the glove is handed in at the draper's; the inquiry sits in the doorway.

papers.text: A working group: is the timetable a form, and must buses fill it in?
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: No bus has filled it in. The group asks for a clerk at every stop.
papers.note: Other: the group meets on the pavement outside the shops.

papers.text: None of our pens write. A working group will report in spotters' pencil.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The report is too faint to read. A second report, in crayon?
papers.note: Owned gag: pens that do not write. Other: the pencils are the spotters'.

papers.text: Plant the year's first bean for the camera. Bertram knows which end.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Other: a little put out at the favour (gossip).

papers.text: A committee on ribbon colours. After eleven meetings: beige.
papers.subject: ribbons
papers.biggerStudy: A second beige has come to light. The committee must meet again.
papers.note: Other: the Society's rosettes must match the openings' ribbon.

papers.text: A working group on picnic weather: nine meetings, one picnic.
papers.subject: picnic-weather
papers.biggerStudy: The picnic weather group asks to meet indoors, for accuracy.
papers.note: Other: it meets on the shops' pavement.

papers.text: Forms for requesting your autograph. I have printed ten thousand.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Your name on each rosette. Then the cup. Then, quietly, the show.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: An umbrella, left at your desk. Not forgotten: left. For when it rains.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the umbrella I left: it would like to be listed as a bus stop.

clippings.sign: UMBRELLA LISTED AS BUS STOP; NO BUS STOPS AT IT
clippings.refuse: UMBRELLA NOT A STOP. IT WAITS BY THE DESK

papers.note: Owned gag: umbrellas left at the desk. The favour puts the spotters out (their timetable).

papers.text: A ribbon, already cut, to save you time. Hundreds more, uncut. No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the ribbon: it wishes to be tied round the prize pumpkin.

clippings.sign: PUMPKIN WEARS YOUR RIBBON; SOCIETY UNTIES IT NIGHTLY
clippings.refuse: RIBBON RETURNED, STILL CUT. NO REASON GIVEN

papers.note: Callback: 'No reason', the first basket. The favour puts the Society out.
